questions.q: Why do this project's non-functional requirements rule out a pure nightly-batch design?
options: Same-day freshness, surviving traffic spikes, and never losing an event together demand something faster and more resilient than a once-a-day batch job
The functional requirements alone rule it out, not the non-functional ones
Nightly batch is always the wrong choice for any retail system
Batch processing cannot handle sales data under any circumstances
questions.explain: Same-day freshness plus never losing an event plus handling traffic spikes rules out nightly-batch-only before any implementation detail is decided.

questions.q: What grain does this project fix for its fact table, and why fix it now?
options: One row per store per day, decided during the serving layer lesson
One row per customer, decided after the dashboard is built
One row per line item per sale, in-store or online — fixed now because every dimension and downstream transform assumes it, per Lesson 8
Grain doesn't need to be fixed until the wrap-up retrospective
questions.explain: Lesson 8 established that grain must be fixed before schema — this project's grain carries all the way to the medallion gold layer.

questions.q: Why does this project use a hybrid batch-plus-streaming ingestion approach instead of picking just one?
options: Nightly POS exports are naturally batch, but online order events are continuous — a hybrid lets both land in the same bronze layer using the right model for each source
Hybrid designs are always required regardless of the data sources
Batch alone would have been sufficient and the hybrid choice was arbitrary
Streaming alone could not technically ingest POS exports
questions.explain: This mirrors Lesson 5's batch-vs-streaming-vs-hybrid decision and Lesson 6's Lambda architecture shape, applied to a real source mix.

questions.q: Which storage choice fits the raw incoming POS and online order events, per Lesson 4's framework?
options: No storage is needed until the gold layer is built
A spreadsheet export, since the volume is expected to be small
Object storage, as a lakehouse bronze layer — cheap, durable landing for event-shaped data before analytical processing
A transactional OLTP database, since the events need row-level updates immediately
questions.explain: Lesson 4 frames OLTP vs. OLAP vs. object storage as a decision; raw event data lands most naturally in object storage before transformation.

questions.q: What does this lesson leave for Lesson 65 to define precisely?
options: Which region the retail chain operates in
The grain of the fact table
The exact freshness SLA — turning "same-day" into a specific number of hours, once ingestion constraints are known
The entire dashboard's visual design
questions.explain: Lesson 18 covers freshness SLA design directly; this kickoff leaves the precise number for Lesson 65 once the ingestion layer's real constraints are visible.
